A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CS-ARM-BN research and JUMP-CP experiments despite the changed title. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MoA classification experiments, cross-source transfers, label-shift tests, and supplementary ablations in Tables 1–4 and A7–A11.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds comparator results, an uncertainty-based image analysis, and an inference-resolution experiment.

M1.justification: CS-ARM-BN retains the same meta-learning procedure and adaptation using BatchNorm statistics from combined control and perturbed samples. The resolution sweep and ensemble uncertainty analysis are supplementary evaluations, not revisions to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight-class JUMP-CP MoA task, using sources 3 and 8 and transfers to source 6. No additional dataset, population, or classification task is reported. The new uncertainty and resolution analyses do not establish expanded dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: DEYO and ROID are added to the ResNet comparisons in Tables 1–4 and A9. Both already appeared in v1's LeViT comparison, Table A10, whose comparator set remains unchanged. This extends existing comparator coverage without replacing the baseline suite.

E3.justification: Appendix C changes the stated training preprocessing from resizing to cropping at 256×256. Appendix I adds an evaluation that varies inference crop resolution while holding the trained model fixed. Existing splits, training budgets, and accuracy metrics remain unchanged; the preprocessing revision does not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendices H and I add two bounded analyses: inspection of atypical images using predictive uncertainty and sensitivity to inference resolution. Existing small-batch, matched-control-count, LeViT, and alignment-level analyses are retained. DEYO and ROID also extend the existing label-shift comparisons.

E5.justification: Appendix H newly estimates per-image predictive uncertainty using the entropy of mean probabilities from an ensemble formed from cross-validation folds and repeated training runs. This adds an uncertainty estimation procedure without documenting additional runs. Existing mean-and-standard-deviation reporting and run counts remain unchanged.

E6.justification: DEYO/ROID result rows and uncertainty/resolution findings are added. TENT and some AdaBN scores are revised: Table 2's S8→S3 TENT result changes from 0.768±0.001 to 0.785±0.008, placing it above unchanged CS-ARM-BN at 0.776±0.016. Table 4's CS-ARM-BN S8→S3 result at α=0.01 changes from 0.770±0.045 to 0.730±0.015. Figures A3–A4 associate artifacts with higher uncertainty and report increasing accuracy with larger crops. These are reported revisions, not established same-protocol performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds explicit mathematical definitions of DeYO's PLPD score and weighted entropy objective, equations 15–16. This is limited formalization of a comparator. The proposed method's assumptions and bias–variance derivations remain unchanged, moving from Appendix F to G; notation corrections do not change that reasoning.

C1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's assertion of being the first to close the domain gap and emphasizes stabilization under small batches and label shift. Its conclusion qualifies near-closure as applying to the evaluated MoA settings. The three introduction contributions and central control-stabilized adaptation claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations concerning controls from different cell lines, potential benefits of pooling images within wells, and evaluation on compounds with strong rather than subtle effects. It adds interpretations of uncertainty and resolution findings and explains the restricted BEN comparison. The earlier speculative three-component explanation for closing the domain gap is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies full-plate processing, three adaptation updates per plate, and learning rate 0.001 for TENT, DEYO, and ROID. Appendix C newly specifies 256×256 center crops at inference. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings. Hardware, selected hyperparameters in Table A5, and code/data access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds a formal CellPainting Gallery reference for a resource already linked in v1 and expands descriptions of the already-cited DEYO and ROID methods. It also withdraws the abstract's first-to-demonstrate gap-closure positioning. The remaining related-work coverage is substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are substantially rewritten, and Section 6 is reorganized around discussion and limitations. Several baseline descriptions move from Section 2.1 into new Appendix D, overlapping pseudocode is consolidated in the appendix, and an Impact Statement is added. Together these substantially revise the narrative framing and organization.

P2.justification: The opening performance chart is removed, with its results retained in Table 1. Existing domain and method diagrams are relocated and renumbered. Figures A3–A4 add an uncertainty image grid and resolution analysis; comparison tables gain rows and Table 1 gains an explanatory footnote. The overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the main ResNet comparisons with DEYO/ROID, makes applicability limits more explicit, and adds useful diagnostic analyses and implementation details. Its narrower claims better match the evaluated setting. These are incremental gains: the core method and most evidence remain unchanged, while sparse setup information for the new diagnostics and unexplained score/preprocessing revisions limit the improvement in evidential clarity.
